lean.fidelity_note: For the common construction of Theorem 7.1, the formal statement produces a smooth odd periodic Euler solution on $[0,T_\infty)$ with mean-zero pressure. The initial data converge in every $C^{m,1/2}$, and convergence in that spatial norm is uniform on every $[0,S]$ with $S<T_\infty$. It then says that any maximal solution of finite lifespan from the same datum lasts at least to $T_\infty$ and agrees with this limit. The paper instead starts with the maximal solution supplied by general existence theory, whose lifespan may still be infinite at this point. Thus the preterminal existence and convergence conclusions are present, but general maximal-solution existence is not asserted by this declaration. Corollary 8.3 subsequently proves finite maximality for the constructed solution. Fields are period-one functions on $\mathbb R^3$; the spatial Hölder norm is $\sum_{i\le m}(\sup|D^if|+[D^if]_{1/2})$, with $D^if$ the full $i$th derivative tensor.

statements.markdown: **Proposition 8.1.** The data $U_j(0)$ converge in every $C^{m,1/2}$ to an odd divergence-free field $u_0$. In particular, $u_0\in C^\infty(\mathbb T^3;\mathbb R^3)$. Let $u$ be the maximal smooth solution of the Euler equations from $u_0$, with maximal time $T_*>0$, supplied by Section 1. Then $T_*\ge T_\infty$ and, for every $T<T_\infty$ and integer $m\ge0$, $U_j\to u$ in $C([0,T];C^{m,1/2})$. The solution is smooth and odd on $[0,T_\infty)\times\mathbb T^3$.
